text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Male taxi drivers in Oslo feel discriminated because they get a 300 crown fine if they wear shorts on the job. Female drivers are allowed to wear skirts. Oslo is experiencing a heatwave with temperatures close to 30 degrees Centigrade.

- Norway falls in fifth place in the World Competitiveness Yearbook compiled by Swiss management school IMD in Lausanne. Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg says the criteria for the study were very diverse, showing that it is not only the oil industry that has put Norway where it is today.
- The number of tourists visiting Trondheim in northern Norway this year has increased by 70 percent compared with 1996.
- Violations of the Health and Safety at Work Act are on the increase in the construction industry in Oslo. Activities on 34 building sites have been stopped so far this year.

- In the latest report on the Nordic mobil phone market, Morgan Stanley gives NetCom a strong buy recommendation. Morgan Stanley believes NetCom's share price will increase to 100 crowns. The share closed at 82 crowns on Tuesday.

- The eastern expansion of the European Union will create problems for Norwegian fish exports. Possible new EU members buy Norwegian fish worth 700 million crowns a year. When these countries become EU members in a few years, these exports will come under new tariffs.

- Canal Digital Norge AS, owned by state telecommunications group Telenor and French Canal Plus, will start in October offering digital TV to Norwegian households via satellite. Espen Asheim, head of Canal Digital, says it is estimated that 30,000 to 45,000 households will buy digital receivers in the next two years.
